scope: Six canonical Form Finding halls; final-text companion illustrations.

plates.title: WHERE DOES DOWNHILL TAKE YOU?
plates.subtitle: Descent
plates.focus: Local cost differences select steps, not velocity; initial address, threshold, frame and budget determine distinct endings.
plates.summary: A gold point takes local steps across a blue drawing. Two beginnings find different valleys; the visitor’s overview never enters the update by itself.
plates.footer: Nothing in the arithmetic establishes that this measure contains everything worth keeping.
panels: Before pressing it, choose where you think the point will go.

Adult visitor beside existing blue cost-surface table, fingertip poised over STEP; one gold marker above blue bowl, companion looking. Pink local-direction arrow lies horizontally over plot, not a gravitational force. No visitor standing or climbing on the blue mesh.
This is already a departure from Forces. There is no stored velocity here.

Small SCHEMATIC inset shows one gold point's previous and current locations with shortening discrete steps toward bowl centre, never an inertial ballistic path. Tiny rule 'proposed = point - rate * gradient(point)'. Hand presses STEP. No new mass, force or velocity variables.
Both runs can stop at a small slope. They do not arrive at the same cost.

Before/after comparison on SAME unequal two-valley surface, two separated SCHEMATIC cards START A / START B, each one gold marker and own short trail ending in a different basin. Both labels SMALL SLOPE; one basin visibly lower. Comparisons are separate runs, not simultaneous markers in one experiment. No exact cost values or invented held-comparison control.
That knowledge has not entered the algorithm merely because it has entered your view.

Visitor walks to side of table and sees the lower valley beyond a ridge; gold point stays in other higher basin. Viewer line of sight indicated gently, no trail hopping ridge, no claim seeing steers marker. Museum bodies and table prominent rather than large extra dashboard.
These endings answer different questions.

Three compact SCHEMATIC condition cards near existing console: SMALL SLOPE local arrows short; LEFT FRAME proposed dashed step goes beyond border while last valid gold point remains INSIDE; STEP LIMIT finite trail ends with a budget icon. Clearly distinct stopping rules, no endpoint declared global solution.
The height makes cost legible across a table.

Wide quiet view adult and older companion beside blue surface above table. Small height relation card 'display height = 0.40 + 0.22 × cost'. Height explains display, not gravitational energy or a walkable terrain. Only established existing artifacts in background; no human travelling on mesh.
plates.source_review: A single schematic landscape overlays the histories of two separate runs; it is not a simultaneous-run mode or a new museum control. Plot height and arrow length are display choices. The main table view selects a rugged landscape while the step inset explains the bowl case; the page is not a temporal record of switching landscapes.

plates.title: DRAWN, EVALUATED, SETTLED
plates.subtitle: Catenary
plates.focus: Hand-drafted sag, analytic catenary and fixed parametric surfaces differ from physical relaxation; resemblance does not supply a load test.
plates.summary: A hand redraws a cable. Washing lines become mirrored arches; a sampled catenoid can be carried without its rings becoming solver controls.
plates.footer: The washing and the cathedral share a curve. They do not yet share a test.
panels: Your hand changes the constraints of that drawing.

Four cyan control beads joined by magenta-to-blue cable. Visitor moves ONE interior bead; same endpoint beads remain fixed for this action. Previous curve faint dashed reference, current curve redraws through four beads with authored sag per span. EXACTLY four beads, not heavy linked physical chain. Tiny label DRAFTED SPLINE.
No weight has been measured and no rope length conserved.

Closer visitor holds that same interior bead, companion eyes follow curve. Small SCHEMATIC card two downward Bezier handles per span suggesting authored sag; label FIXED SAG RULE. No tension measurement, weight scale or length-preserving lock. Do not add an actual hanging physics chain as if live.
The washing and the cathedral share a curve. They do not yet share a test.

Existing laundry display: three end-supported sagging lines with bright flat shirts/towels, and above EACH line the same curve mirrored upward as pale ghost arch. Ends align vertically between downward and upward copies. Clothes add no deformation/load. Compare reference material but light warm museum style, no actual cathedral constructed.
The formula does not choose its own boundary.

Visitor studies low broad CYAN WIREFRAME CATENOID: rotational hourglass OPEN AT BOTH ENDS, circular rims, fixed waist; small card 'r = c × cosh(u/c)' / 'chosen range of u'. Broad squat shape, not tall vase; no new boundary sliders or stretching rings.
The opening travels with it; the sampled mesh retains its shape.

Visitor lifts and turns same fixed squat open catenoid in hand. Clearly hollow circular opening visible, rim scale unchanged through turn. Ghost before-pose only small schematic. No deforming film, collapsed discs or changing separation.
There is still work between having an object and having an instrument for it.

Low small GREEN WIREFRAME HELICOID on plinth beside cyan catenoid, both sampled fixed models. Visitor looks between two shapes and nearby screen whose small label NO COMPATIBLE LIVE MEASUREMENT is readable. No morphing animation between catenoid and helicoid; do not fabricate scanner data.
plates.source_review: The laundry arches mirror analytic curves; the clothes do not add load. Carried catenoid and helicoid remain fixed sampled models. Their mathematical association is not depicted as an implemented deformation or physical stability test.

plates.title: WHAT A BUDGET LEAVES
plates.subtitle: Relaxation
plates.focus: Finite constraint passes alter agreement; live cloth, frozen rocking lattice and retained glass vessel keep different histories. Transparency differs from collision.
plates.summary: The cloth continues while a lattice carries one solved pose and glass keeps another. A small average can leave a large local error hidden.
plates.footer: The cloth keeps changing. The vessel keeps a moment, and the surface of that moment keeps a boundary.
panels: The cloth continues; the lattice and the vessel keep the pose reached after a chosen number of steps.

Adult and older companion enter existing room: magenta cloth suspended from TWO top corners at bench, cropped cyan-wire/pink-mass lattice, tall pale-cyan glass vessel. Static glass contrasted with live cloth by two faint successive cloth poses, not by shaking glass. No exact full grid count asserted.
More passes give those relations another chance to agree.

Visitor at cloth PASSES console with WIND OFF. Two small SCHEMATIC temporal cards ONE PASS / FOUR PASSES each show same pinned corners and connected cloth patch under gravity. This change restarts experiment, not mid-run immediate transformation. Tiny label SAME START · MORE CORRECTIONS; no new held-display mode.
The average has become small while one local relation is still far from its request.

Close-up cropped connected cloth springs, one length still noticeably stretched. Board says MEAN / WORST with labels AVERAGE AGREEMENT / LARGEST LOCAL ERROR, no fabricated exact live percentages. Highlight worst spring without implying worst necessarily increases with more passes. Visitor compares local relation with overall drape.
The rocking carries a frozen result

Cropped lattice bench shown BEFORE TILT / AFTER TILT in little schematic: identical distances between pink nodes and cyan wires, whole lattice rotated as rigid display pose. label SOLVER ALREADY STOPPED. Not ongoing internal deformation, no wind solver asserted.
Transparency offers a view, not an entrance.

Actual reference glass vessel tall faceted pale cyan closed pear/amphora-like body, background visible through it. Visitor stands OUTSIDE it, looks through toward cloth beyond; simple SCHEMATIC collision envelope closed around vase. No doorway, walking inside glass or hand-tracking collision claim.
The clock is part of the genome here.

Visitor and companion contemplate the single kept vessel on simple plinth. Tiny illustration card INPUT CONDITIONS → 200 STEPS → KEPT POSE, decorative silhouettes not a live control bank. The glass does not resume falling; no stiffness or duration knobs available on vessel. Beautiful light catches frozen facets.
plates.source_review: Cloth and lattice views are cropped details, not exact node inventories. Mean/worst labels describe different reports without inventing live numbers. Vessel conditions are a source explanation, not exhibit controls; transparency does not remove its closed collision surface.

plates.title: WHERE FORCES CANCEL
plates.subtitle: Equilibrium
plates.focus: An ideal moment balance can be constructed statically; direct scale animation and prescribed tower sway are not load responses.
plates.summary: A mobile makes mass and lever distance readable. A squeezing triangle and a braced tower offer convincing structure without having tested resistance.
plates.footer: A picture of structure is not yet an instrument for its strength.
panels: Start with a balance whose arithmetic you can inspect.

CROPPED DETAIL of large static hanging mobile: painted aluminum discs on thin wires and branch rods. Adult visitor and older companion look up, no hand plucking or motion streaks. Modelled mass plaques attached to discs, symbolic m labels rather than fabricated measured grams. Simple warm museum space.
The heavier child rides the shorter arm because the arithmetic gives it no choice.

Close SCHEMATIC ONE LEVER: larger LEFT disc, smaller RIGHT disc; pivot closer to larger left disc, SHORT left distance dL and LONG right dR, rod LEVEL. Label 'mL × dL = mR × dR'. Two vertical hanging wires, no lever rolling/tilting under applied hand force. No exact inferred sizes or measurements.
The rods and wires have no mass in this calculation.

Visitor follows one branch upward; tiny diagram shows child masses added to parent at branch join, rods/wires distinct faint gray with label NOT COUNTED IN MASS MODEL. Physical visible rods remain, not disappearing; rendered matter differs from assigned mass. Crop larger tree without counting all discs.
The whole object is being scaled: the source writes a sine-driven change directly into its transform.

Nearby triangle THREE struts meeting at THREE orange joints, no cables. Two small SCHEMATIC poses show same triangle scaled shorter/wider on a prescribed sine rhythm. Label TRANSFORM ANIMATION · NO APPLIED LOAD. Do not draw visitor pushing or a spring resisting; the illusion of structural resistance must not become physics.
This construction has not measured either quantity.

Braced steel tower on broad base with orange beacon; visible stacked cross-braced storeys, four corner legs, finer repeated legs along same corners. Caption board RECURSIVE BRACED STOREYS / NO LOAD TEST. Sway marks only whole prescribed pose, no simulated wind or collapse. No tower described as optimum.
Before asking whether a form has reached the bottom, ask what was allowed to move and what counted as success.

Adult and companion between static mobile, triangle and tower, quiet room-level view. Separate small labels ENCODED BALANCE / ANIMATED POSE / UNTESTED LOAD. No new physical experiment performed; objects keep established dispositions. Let art stay beautiful while differences become inspectable.
plates.source_review: The lever inset is symbolic and the mobile view cropped. It depicts an encoded ideal balance with massless members, not dynamic equilibrium or real material strength. Triangle scaling and tower sway remain prescribed transforms.

plates.title: WILLING TO GET WORSE
plates.subtitle: Annealing
plates.focus: Random-neighbour uphill acceptance differs from gradient descent and forced hopping; the two wells stage unequal receivers rather than a shared life measure.
plates.summary: A search accepts an uphill move, then cools. Deep stillness and shallow responsiveness sit beside each other under different conditions.
plates.footer: Reaching the lowest value in a model is not the same as finding the form you want.
panels: A better move is always taken.

Existing dark survey table with glowing regularly corrugated Rastrigin relief and one marker. Adult watches downhill accepted proposal, small SCHEMATIC nearby-neighbour inset current higher dot → lower proposed dot. No gradient arrow or inertia, no temperature represented as actual heat/fire.
A worse move is taken with a probability that depends on how much worse it is and how hot things are.

Same table, SCHEMATIC current dot lower than proposed uphill dot; proposed move highlighted as POSSIBLE, NOT CERTAIN. Tiny rule 'p = exp(−ΔE/T)' and 'UPHILL MAY PASS'. Visitor near START T setting; temperature a search parameter, no source fire or generic neural training diagram.
HOP invokes that relocation directly; it does not ask the acceptance branch for permission.

Close visitor presses HOP. Dashed relocation connects two distant sites on same field labelled FORCED RELOCATION + REHEAT. Separate adjacent text ACCEPTANCE RULE distinguishes random neighbour acceptance. Do not show the HOP as a naturally rolled trajectory across all in-between addresses; no guarantee deepest minimum found.
These are different receivers under different conditions, not two runs of one measured objective.

Adult at OUTSIDE rim of low open tank, companion beside. LEFT deep narrow well has single STATIC cube at bottom; RIGHT broad shallow basin has moving soft green lattice receiving periodic jostle. Small labels STATIC CUBE / DISTURBED LATTICE. Same picture does not make them a matched experiment or a life test. Cube visible down inside; visitor not standing in pit.
The installation has authored those roles; it has not measured a universal boundary between life and rest.

Visitor chooses INTERPRET after observing wells; optional Q proposition revealed on nearby small plaque 'LOW ENOUGH TO HOLD · HIGH ENOUGH TO BE MOVED'. Both wells unchanged, no new living/dead identities or universal meter/score. Bodies have different drives. Small screen diagram is interpretation, not new measurement.
Here the brackets and cables are meshes placed at chosen addresses.

Existing impossible end table: two steel bracket assemblies separated, top not touching base, connected visually by central cable and THREE perimeter cables, teacup atop. Static meshes in a carefully chosen pose. Small label CONSTRUCTED POSE · NO LOAD SOLVER. Adult/companion look through the gap, not pressing top or causing physical suspension.
plates.source_review: The acceptance and HOP insets describe different rules, without drawing a guaranteed best outcome. Wells have unequal drives and no shared measured objective. Q is an authored interpretation; the tension-supported table is a static pose, not a load test.

plates.title: A SHAPE THAT COUNTS
plates.subtitle: Forge
plates.focus: Physical quietness differs from a detector's height-and-time criterion; the point cloud reaches an authored body on a clock; search endings keep distinct reasons.
plates.summary: A useful low stack can be refused. A green cloud gathers into its planned body, while another point follows local slope and leaves a history.
plates.footer: Similar-looking arrivals can conceal very different freedoms.
panels: Both can stop moving, but the puzzle does not treat them as the same result.

Adult puts down small cubes and pyramids on balance platform. Two SCHEMATIC sequential trials: LOW QUIET HEAP, HEIGHT TOO LOW versus TALL QUIET STACK, HEIGHT + STABILITY PASS.
